data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1, approximately exp(-c) with c \u2248 0.1, because the process is a local energy-minimizing flow whose only finite obstructions are non-expanding stable cuts: stable mixed configurations in which every vertex has at least two same-colored neighbors, which on a random 3-regular graph are exactly the 2-regular induced subgraphs (disjoint cycles) with all edges crossing, plus single-edge cuts whose endpoints both have monochromatic remaining pairs. The expected number of disjoint induced cycles with crossing-edge structure is \u0398(1) (girth-3, 4, 5 cycles appear with Poisson counts), so the probability that at least one exists \u2014 and that the flow falls into it \u2014 converges to a Poisson-based constant; in the absence of such cycles consensus is achieved whp by monotone cut-size decrease.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The consensus indicator concentrates over random graph draws (annealed = quenched), which by SRC_016 forces the constant to collapse to 0 or 1","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Basin measure of stable cuts is provably monotone in structural prevalence (SRC_017's refutation condition), eliminating the intermediate regime","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Dynamical trapping structures beyond static stable cuts (e.g., long-lived metastable plateaus with decreasing but non-extinct cut) are shown to carry non-vanishing mass","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A supercritical family of stable cuts (\u0398(n) in expectation) with non-negligible basin is exhibited","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The asynchronous update rule is a monotone descent on the number of crossing (disagreement) edges: a vertex flipping to its neighbors' majority strictly reduces its incident crossing count or leaves it unchanged (flips only occur when the local crossing count strictly decreases, since a vertex with majority-mismatched color has \u22652 crossing edges and after the flip has \u22641). Hence the process absorbs in finite time at a local minimum of the cut functional. The local minima that are NOT global are precisely the locally stable mixed configurations. On a random 3-regular graph, enumerate them: a vertex is 'stable' iff it has \u22652 neighbors of its own color. Removing all crossing edges partitions the graph into monochromatic components; each vertex needs at least 2 same-color edges, so each monochromatic component must contain a cycle or be supported by cut edges with multiplicity \u2014 the only finite obstructions are (i) induced cycles where the cycle's vertices all take one color and their third neighbors take the other (each cycle vertex then has 2 same-color cycle neighbors and 1 crossing), and (ii) a single crossing edge whose endpoints each have their other two neighbors same-colored as themselves. Family (ii) requires two vertices at distance 2 sharing a structure; its count is also \u0398(1) Poisson. Since random 3-regular graphs have only Poisson-many short cycles and these obstructions must be SHORT (long induced cycles with all third-edges exiting exist with exponentially small probability per unit length via expansion), the total obstruction count converges to a Poisson random variable with constant mean c. Consensus probability \u2192 P(no obstruction absorbs the flow) \u2248 exp(-c') for a basin-weighted c' \u2264 c, a constant strictly between 0 and 1.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
